sections.h2: Where is Grant County, Washington, and how did it form?
sections.html:
Grant County sits in central Washington, with Ephrata as the county seat and Moses Lake as the largest city. The state legislature created it on February 24, 1909, carving it out of Douglas County, and named it for Ulysses S. Grant.

According to the county's Wikipedia entry, Grant County covers 2,791 square miles, of which 2,680 is land, making it the fourth-largest county in the state by area. Its neighbors are Douglas County to the north, Okanogan to the northeast, Lincoln and Adams to the east, Franklin to the southeast, Benton to the south, Yakima to the southwest and Kittitas to the west.

Incorporated places include Electric City, Ephrata, George, Grand Coulee, Mattawa, Moses Lake, Quincy, Royal City, Soap Lake and Warden, plus the towns of Coulee City, Coulee Dam (partly), Hartline, Krupp and Wilson Creek. Landmarks that shape where people live include the Columbia River, Moses Lake, Potholes Reservoir, Soap Lake and the Grand Coulee. The Cascades block most coastal rain, which gives the county hot summers and cold winters.

sections.h2: What shapes the Grant County economy and housing stock?
sections.html:
Farming and irrigation drive much of it. Wikipedia reports that Grant County is the top crop-producing county in the state and a large source of Washington's hay, and a sign on I-90 at the county line calls it the nation's leading potato-producing county.

The reason is water. Dryland farming gave way to irrigation after the first large-scale attempts in 1898, and the Columbia Basin Project, built around Grand Coulee Dam, changed the region for good after its approval in 1933. Towns such as Quincy, Ephrata and Wilson Creek grew alongside the railroads that carried crops out.

The 2020 census counted 99,123 residents and 38,635 housing units. About 62.2% of occupied homes were owner-occupied, and 11.8% of all units were vacant. School districts serving the county include Moses Lake, Ephrata, Quincy, Othello, Wahluke, Royal, Soap Lake, Warden, Grand Coulee Dam, Coulee-Hartline, Almira, Odessa and Wilson Creek. Which district a house sits in changes the levies on its tax bill, so check the parcel record before you price it.

sections.h2: Which Grant County offices deal with property tax?
sections.html:
The Assessor values property and the Treasurer bills and collects the tax. The Assessor tracks about 61,570 parcels, keeps ownership and legal descriptions up to date, and does not set the tax amount. Voters, state limits and the assessed value in each district set the rate.

  • Assessor: Courthouse Annex, Room 107, 35 C Street NW, Ephrata. Phone 509-754-2013, weekdays 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The current assessor is Melissa McKnight.
  • Treasurer: 35 C Street NW, Room 204, Ephrata, mailing address P.O. Box 37. Phone 509-754-2010, weekdays 8 a.m. to noon and 1 to 5 p.m.
  • Board of Equalization: hears valuation appeals. The Assessor's Office, at 509-754-2011 ext. 2683, helps owners find comparable sales.

The Treasurer's page links to a searchable tax statement for 2025 and 2026, and a parcel lookup, so you can pull a payoff picture without visiting. Mailing address changes and the quit claim forms mentioned below also go through that office.

sections.h2: How does the Grant County Assessor value a house?
sections.html:
Real property is valued as of January 1, and the Assessor revalues properties every year. The county's FAQ says you need to file a new petition each year to protect your appeal rights, because a prior-year appeal does not carry over.

Two programs have dates worth knowing if you own an older home or farmland. Senior and disabled tax deferral applications are due April 1 under state law, while claims for the senior and disabled exemption are accepted all year for taxes payable the following year. Open space (current use) applications are deemed approved on May 1 unless the Assessor says otherwise, and the window to apply for the next year's valuation runs from January 1 through December 31.

The Assessor's page lists a senior exemption press release for the 2027 tax year. Ask the office for the current income limit before you rely on any figure.

sections.h2: What are the key Grant County property tax dates?
sections.html:
First-half tax is due April 30 and second-half tax is due October 31, and the Treasurer accepts a postmark from the post office. Late payments pick up interest, and some property types pick up penalties as well.

DateWhat happens
January 1Valuation date for real property
April 1Senior and disabled deferral applications due
April 30First half of taxes due
June 13% penalty on delinquent tax, where state law applies it
July 1Last day to petition the Board of Equalization, or 30 days after the notice if later
October 31Second half due (a Saturday in 2026)
December 1Additional 8% penalty on delinquent tax, where state law applies it

Source: Grant County Assessor's important dates and RCW 84.56.020. The penalties do not apply to residential property of four or fewer units, which pays interest only, set at 9% a year for taxes levied in 2023 and later. Other property pays 12% a year plus the two penalties.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Grant County assessment?
sections.html:
Start by calling the Assessor, then file a petition with the Grant County Board of Equalization. It must arrive by July 1 of the assessment year or within 30 calendar days after the date of the value change notice, whichever is later, and a mailed petition must be postmarked by then. Filing is free, and each parcel needs its own petition.

  • Include the parcel number, your name and address, a property description, the Assessor's value, your opinion of value and your reasons, signed and dated, with a copy of the notice.
  • Add comparable sales, repair estimates, an appraisal or photos. The Board weighs sales closest to January 1.
  • Submit extra evidence at least 21 business days before the hearing.

The assessor's value is presumed correct, and you carry the burden of showing otherwise with clear, cogent and convincing evidence. Hardship and the size of the tax bill cannot be considered. You get at least 30 business days' notice of the hearing, and decisions usually arrive within about two weeks, though the statute allows 45 days. Either side can appeal to the state Board of Tax Appeals within 30 days of the decision.

sections.h2: How do you pay Grant County taxes, and what if you are behind?
sections.html:
Pay by mail, in person or through Point & Pay. Online fees are 2.7% for credit cards, 0.95% for debit and $1.30 for an eCheck, and a returned payment carries a $30 fee. Payments can take three to five business days to show.

The Treasurer posts a delinquent tax payment plan application and an interest waiver application for a principal residence heading into foreclosure. The office also runs an annual tax foreclosure sale: the 2026 sale was held November 9 and 10 on the Public Surplus website, so it has already taken place. If your tax is far behind, call the Treasurer on 509-754-2010 well before any sale date, since state law allows an income-qualified owner living in the home to seek a waiver of interest and penalties shortly before the third anniversary of delinquency.

sections.h2: What happens at closing when you sell a Grant County house?
sections.html:
The deed and a real estate excise tax affidavit go to the Treasurer in the county where the property sits. The Treasurer's page links the state forms, the exemption code list and a lack of probate affidavit used with a deed when no probate was opened.

The Department of Revenue says the seller usually pays this tax and it is due on the date of sale. State thresholds are graduated by price, and a local rate is added, so ask the Treasurer for the combined rate that applies to your city. Blank deed and quit claim forms are listed there too, and a title company or attorney can draft a deed if yours needs one.

faqs.q: When are Grant County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Half is due April 30 and the other half October 31. The Treasurer accepts a postmark from the post office, and any amount still unpaid after the dates carries interest.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Grant County assessment?
faqs.a: Until July 1 of the assessment year or 30 calendar days after the value change notice, whichever is later. Mailed petitions must be postmarked by that date, and filing costs nothing.

faqs.q: Does Grant County revalue homes every year?
faqs.a: Yes. The Assessor revalues properties each year, and you must file a fresh petition each year to protect your appeal rights.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to pay Grant County taxes online?
faqs.a: Credit cards carry 2.7%, debit cards 0.95% and eChecks $1.30. Checks by mail or in person carry no vendor fee.

faqs.q: Was there a Grant County tax foreclosure sale in 2026?
faqs.a: Yes. The Treasurer held it on November 9 and 10 on the Public Surplus website, so it has passed. Contact the Treasurer at 509-754-2010 about the next one.
